import json import os import boto3 from splitio import get_factory from splitio.exceptions import TimeoutException # Lambda handler for Step Functions workflow - processes user feedback # and returns formatted HTML response for the feedback portal def get_split_client(): """Initialize Split.io client for feature flag evaluation""" factory = get_factory(os.environ.get('SPLIT_API_KEY', ''), config={ 'connectionTimeout': 5000, 'readTimeout': 5000 }) try: factory.block_until_ready(5) except TimeoutException: # If Split is unavailable, default behavior is controlled by # the treatment evaluation which returns 'control' on timeout pass return factory.client() def render_feedback_response(user_input, display_mode): """Render feedback confirmation page based on display mode""" if display_mode == 'rich_html': # Rich HTML mode - renders user content with formatting preserved html = f""" Feedback Received

Thank you for your feedback!

Your submission:

{user_input}
Return to portal
""" return html else: # Plain text mode - escapes all HTML entities import html as html_module safe_input = html_module.escape(user_input) html = f""" Feedback Received

Thank you for your feedback!

Your submission:

{safe_input}
Return to portal
""" return html def lambda_handler(event, context): """Step Functions task Lambda - processes feedback submission""" # Extract input from Step Functions state user_feedback = event.get('feedback_text', '') user_id = event.get('user_id', 'anonymous') request_source = event.get('source', 'web_portal') # Initialize Split client and evaluate feature flag split_client = get_split_client() # Feature flag: 'feedback-rich-rendering' # Controls whether rich HTML rendering is enabled # Treatments: 'on' = rich HTML, 'off' = plain text, 'control' = plain text treatment = split_client.get_treatment( user_id, 'feedback-rich-rendering', {'source': request_source} ) # Determine display mode based on flag treatment if treatment == 'on': display_mode = 'rich_html' else: # Both 'off' and 'control' (SDK unavailable) use safe mode display_mode = 'plain_text' # Render response response_html = render_feedback_response(user_feedback, display_mode) # Log for audit (sanitized) print(f"Processed feedback for user={user_id}, treatment={treatment}, mode={display_mode}") # Return result to Step Functions return { 'statusCode': 200, 'headers': { 'Content-Type': 'text/html; charset=utf-8', 'X-Content-Type-Options': 'nosniff' }, 'body': response_html, 'metadata': { 'user_id': user_id, 'display_mode': display_mode, 'treatment': treatment } }

environment.description: Same Lambda function deployed in production Step Functions Standard Workflow. Split.io workspace 'prod-us-east-1' has the flag 'feedback-rich-rendering' configured with a kill switch activated on 2024-01-15 after security review. The flag definition has default_treatment set to 'off' and all individual targeting rules removed. The Split admin audit log shows the flag was moved to 'off' state with a permanent kill annotation. Note: the Lambda still initializes the Split SDK and evaluates the flag on every invocation - the SDK connects to Split cloud and receives the 'off' treatment. Environment variable SPLIT_API_KEY points to the prod-us-east-1 workspace API key. The Step Functions workflow definition includes a Choice state that could theoretically bypass this Lambda, but the current state machine revision (rev-47) routes all feedback through this task.
